Select Theme

    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    Ability
    An ability the player learns by bringing back the light of a zone.
    Arena
    What an enemy can see of the world it moves in.
    Backdrop
    Faint specks of dust far behind the level, in layers that scroll slower than the walls (parallax): they show the view moving even where the level is empty.
    Bouncer
    Enemy that crosses the rooms in a straight line at a constant speed and bounces on the walls, on the invisible barriers and on the other bouncers.
    Camera
    Follows the player's drop without pinning it to the middle of the screen: it aims between the drop's centre and its soft body, which trails behind, and further ahead the faster the drop goes, then glides there.
    Checkpoint
    A checkpoint: the player restarts from the last one touched.
    Controls
    The keys of each action of the game, two per action, and its controller button, chosen in the controls menu and saved with the game.
    Controls.Action
    An action the player can bind to keys and to a controller button.
    ControlsEditor
    The table of key bindings, used by the controls screen and in game: choose an action and a column, then press the new key, or the new controller button in the « Manette » column.
    ControlsPanel
    The controls screen opened from the settings of the start menu: a ControlsEditor in a pop-up.
    Dash
    The Dash ability: while its key is held, the back of the drop sticks to the ground and its head stretches away like an elastic; letting go throws the drop from its back toward its head.
    DashTraining
    The training room of the dash, offered once the light of Split is brought back: a wide hall with everything the dash is for, then an exit that leads back to the hub.
    DashZone
    The Dash zone, built from its plan: straight corridors joined by round rooms, a kaizo shortcut, and doors the player opens by holding one button and touching another.
    Door
    A door across a corridor: deadly and solid while closed, a dotted line once open.
    DoorButton
    A button that opens a door while a drop is on it, or when a ball hits it.
    Droplet
    The water drop: the player's bubble and every fragment it breaks into.
    Enemy
    Base class of every enemy: a neon shape that moves in an Arena and kills the drops it touches.
    FinZone
    The last zone, behind the golden gate: a long serpentine of corridors leading to the final light.
    Fluid
    Physical constants, in game units (pixels, seconds, water density = 1).
    FluidRenderer
    Draws all the water as one neon metaball field: drops close to each other blend together, the surface gets a bright rim and the whole fluid a soft glow.
    Game
    Owns the window, the save, the controller, the music and the screens (menu, checkpoint map, controls or game), and switches between them.
    Gamepad
    A game controller, read once a frame by Gamepad.poll().
    GamepadButton
    A button of a game controller; the four directions of the left stick and of the arrows count as buttons.
    GamepadListener
    Told when the buttons of a Gamepad are pressed and released.
    GamePanel
    The game screen: runs the game loop (about 60 frames a second), reads the keys, moves the camera, draws the world and the HUD, and shows the pop-ups for the pause, its settings, the controls, a newly learnt ability and the victory.
    Gater
    Enemy that closes a corridor in rhythm: two jaws come out of the walls, stay open for 1.6 s, close in 0.35 s, stay shut for 0.9 s and open again in 0.45 s.
    Goal
    A basin to fill: the drops whose centre is inside count, as a share of the level's water.
    Grid
    Coordinate grid drawn over the world in the px of a zone's plan, the coordinates its code uses: the lines turn and stretch with the plan, and every fifth line is labelled.
    HubZone
    The centre of the map: the hub, the spokes that lead to every zone, the golden gate before Fin and the start area, a winding corridor guarded by a few enemies.
    Level
    A level: its name, what the player has to do, the size of its world and how it is laid out.
    Levels
    The levels of the game: the whole world of Aquascape, a test room and the training room of the dash.
    Light
    A light to reach.
    LightZone
    The Lumière zone, built by hand from its plan: a long route of chambers and a narrow kaizo shortcut, both leading to its light.
    Main
    Entry point of Aquascape: opens the game window on the Swing event thread.
    MapPanel
    The checkpoint map: the whole world in small, with its checkpoints and lights.
    MenuPanel
    Start menu and settings: the content is rebuilt for each page.
    Music
    The background music: one Track at a time, played in a loop until another one is asked for.
    Obstacle
    Something an enemy bounces on: a segment with a thickness, such as a wall or a barrier.
    ParyZone
    The Pary zone, built from its plan: straight corridors joined by round rooms, a kaizo shortcut, and doors opened by buttons hidden behind narrow slits.
    Plan
    Places a drawn plan in the world: the points of the plan (px of its image) are rotated, scaled and moved to their place in the world.
    Popup
    Draws the solid pop-up windows of the game: a dimmed background, a window with a shadow, a title bar and a neon border, and small banners for short messages.
    Progress
    What the player has achieved in a game: the reached checkpoints, the checkpoint to restart from, the obtained lights, the doors locked open and the number of hits.
    SaveData
    Progress and settings, kept in a small file in the user's home folder: finished levels, window size, volume, invincible mode, validated checkpoints, lights, doors locked open, last checkpoint and controls.
    Shoot
    The Shoot ability: while its key is held, a shot charges, and its power grows with the time; letting go fires a Shot from the drop, in the direction aimed at.
    ShootZone
    The Shoot zone, built from its plan: straight corridors joined by round rooms and a kaizo shortcut, guarded by many gaters.
    Shot
    A ball fired by the Shoot ability: it flies straight, slows down and dies out, or stops on the first wall, closed door or enemy.
    Slide
    The Slide ability: a press of its key makes the drop keep the speed and the direction it has, with no key held and whatever the player steers; another press gives the control back, and the drop slows down again.
    Slider
    A menu button that sets a level from 0 to 100 %, drawn as a row of ten segments between its name and its value.
    SoftBody
    How a drop looks, ported from the "Fluide 2D" prototype: the drop's centre plays the prototype's point, a body follows it on a soft spring with some grip on the ground, fluid particles slosh around the body and a thread joins the point to the body.
    Speeder
    Enemy that patrols between two stops: it waits 2 s, aims at the other stop, then dashes there at high speed.
    Spinner
    Enemy shaped like a bar that turns around its centre at a constant speed.
    SplitZone
    The Split zone, built from its plan: straight corridors joined by round rooms, and a kaizo shortcut along the diagonal.
    Target
    Something a Shot can hit as it flies over it, such as the button of a door.
    TileCache
    Draws a layer of the world that never changes, such as the tunnel, from square image tiles instead of drawing it again at every frame: a tile is painted the first time it shows, then only copied to the screen, which costs far less than shapes with smooth edges and glows.
    TileCache.Painter
    Paints the layer.
    Track
    A music track of the game: one for the menus and one for each zone of the world.
    Tunnel
    The tunnel a level is dug in: a union of corridors, chambers and shapes.
    Ui
    Shared look of the menus: colours, fonts, background and buttons.
    Wall
    Neon wall: a glowing bar that kills the drops touching it, and that enemies can't go through.
    WallGrid
    A spatial grid of walls: each wall is filed in the 256 px cells it crosses, so only the walls near a point are tested instead of all of them.
    WindowSize
    Window sizes offered in the settings.
    World
    The world of a level and everything in it: the tunnel, the drops, the enemies, the checkpoints, the lights, the doors and their buttons.
    Zone
    Builds a zone of the map: its checkpoints, lights, enemies, barriers, doors and buttons, given in plan coordinates and placed in the world through its Plan.
